audit.why: 50.64% over 4433 games is a true even lane and the difficulty label matches. The shape is a bow: Katarina bullies a pre-3 Fizz, Fizz owns levels 6 through first item, and Katarina takes the game back in 2+ item teamfights.
audit.corrected: Label unchanged; the chart now carries that shape instead of reading 'Skill' on all seven rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer phases[N].side read 'Skill' while the content layer and packet both read Katarina/Katarina/Katarina/Katarina/Fizz/Fizz/Katarina.
audit.why: Playful / Trickster is 16s at rank 1 and only 8s at rank 5, so the early punish window is enormous and shrinks as the game goes; Chum the Waters at 120s rank 1 and 1300 range is what makes levels 6 through first item his; his single-target pattern is what gives the 2+ item fights back to Katarina.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side -> Katarina, phases[4..5].side -> Fizz, phases[6].side -> Katarina, ratings moved with them, and phases[4].why / phases[5].why rewritten in the same proposal because their verdict flipped. win[0..6] already holds these values on disk.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit; dosFull[1].d was tradeGood pasted under 'Blink to daggers, not targets'; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad pasted under 'Fight away from your steel'; dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second invitation' when E is 16/14/12/10/8.
audit.why: Two interactions decide the matchup and both are in Riot's text. Playful / Trickster makes Fizz untargetable, so it does not merely dodge burst — it eats an entire Death Lotus while the channel keeps running. Chum the Waters knocks the target up, and Katarina's R is flagged channel-interruptible, so the shark ends the spin outright. The third, missing entirely, is that Seastone Trident empowers his NEXT attack, making the wind-up the burst tell rather than the cast.
audit.corrected: All three written: the untargetable-eats-Lotus rule in tradeBad and report[5].t, the shark knockup in breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[2].d, the W wind-up tell in dosFull[1].d and report[5].t.
sources: enemyKit Fizz E/W/R text and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no number, and three fields understated the punish window as '8 seconds' or 'fifteen seconds' when Playful / Trickster is 16s at rank 1.
audit.why: The whole early game is 'how long is he defenceless after E'. At rank 1 that is 16 seconds, not 8 — the page was telling a reader to take half the window they actually have.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[2].d, whys[2], spikes[0].text and the content mid field all now carry 16s at rank 1 / 8s at rank 5.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fields claimed E costs him 'half his damage' — a magnitude with no source in the kit.
audit.why: Riot's text does not quantify how much of his damage sits in E. Directionally right is not right, and the real, checkable fact — that a spent E leaves him with no dodge and no escape for up to 16 seconds — is stronger advice anyway.
audit.corrected: 'half damage' / 'half his damage' replaced with the cooldown fact in whys[2] and spikes[0].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave used the placeholder 'a CC mage's tower'; Fizz is not a CC mage.
audit.why: The real wave rule is that a pre-3 Fizz cannot contest a shoved wave at all, and that after 6 a freeze near his tower gives him a shark angle onto a stationary target.

audit.whatIsWrong: The brief's missingInteractions claims 'Both sides carry displacement (Preparation (W) vs Chum the Waters (R))'. Katarina's W does not displace anyone.
audit.why: Riot's text for Katarina's W is a burst of move speed and a dagger tossed into the air above herself. The knockup flag on it is a tooltip-parsing misfire, and writing 'whoever lands the displacement first owns the trade' would tell a reader Katarina has a knockup she does not have. Also note the 'grounding' flags on Fizz's E and R are unsupported by Riot's text and were not written.
audit.corrected: Only Fizz's knockup is claimed, and only as the thing that ends Death Lotus.
sources: ownerKit Katarina W text vs flags
enemyKit Fizz E/R text vs flags

edits.before: Levels 3-5 the lane is a cooldown chess game you're favored in: E Playful/Trickster is his trade, his dodge, and his escape all at once. Never engage into it — poke until he uses it to dodge a Q or farm, then Shunpo and unload the full 8-ish seconds it's down. notes: Chart: full layer read 'Skill' on all seven rows against a content layer and packet that agree on Katarina x4 / Fizz / Fizz / Katarina. Sides moved to match; win[0..6] already correct on disk, and phases[4].why and phases[5].why were rewritten in the same proposal because they flipped to Fizz. Number defects fixed beyond the lint: the punish window after Playful / Trickster was written as '8 seconds' or 'fifteen seconds' in four places when it is 16s at rank 1, and 'half his damage' was a magnitude with no source in Riot's text. REJECTED the brief's 'both sides carry displacement' interaction — Katarina's W has a knockup derived flag that contradicts Riot's description (move speed plus a dagger tossed above herself), so she has no displacement here; likewise the 'grounding' flags on Fizz's E and R are unsupported by his ability text and nothing was written from them.
